subject: Post-demo: prompt/output persistence, residency, and retention — next steps & MOP
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@medpath.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: prompt/output persistence, residency, and retention — next steps & MOP

Hi Lydia — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a proposed mutual action plan so we can move the Sec/Legal review forward. Attaching a draft retention matrix (redwood-retention-matrix-v1.xlsx) and our SOC 2 summary.

Highlights from the call (short):
- Product: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC).
- Question: what prompt/response/trace data do we persist, where, and for how long (PII considerations).
- Next step: I can provide a table mapping exactly which fields are stored by each deployment mode + default TTLs and customizable options.

Quick answers up front (high level):
- Hosted (default): prompts/outputs are ephemeral by default; we persist minimal telemetry for 30 days for debugging/ratelimiting.
- Dedicated: default trace retention 90 days; configurable shorter/longer via contract.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): storage location and retention are customer-controlled; Redwood can run the control plane while data-at-rest stays in your environment.
- Audit logs: stored and searchable for 365 days by default across hosted/dedicated; can be exported to your SIEM.
- Encryption & keys: AES-256 at rest; KMS/HSM integrations for Private.
- Optional quality monitoring: if you opt in, we will persist prompts & outputs for model quality monitoring; retention is configurable — default 90 days.

Action items I propose:
1) I’ll send the detailed retention matrix (attached) and a short description of what each log/trace contains.
2) Karthik — can you confirm the SOC 2 package we should send and whether we need a customer NDA before sharing the full report?
3) Lydia — please confirm which residency requirement (US, EU) you need for stored prompts/outputs and whether MedPath requires automatic PII redaction (we offer server-side redaction rules and customer-side pipelines).

Proposed timeline: we’ll share the retention matrix by EOD tomorrow, you review and flag any rows to tighten, then we publish a mutually agreed retention policy for the POC.

Attachments: redwood-retention-matrix-v1.xlsx (stub), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (stub).

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: prompt/output persistence, residency, and retention — next steps & MOP

Thanks Sean — good recap. A couple of clarifying questions before we loop Legal/Security:

1) Exactly which of the following are persisted in each deployment mode: full prompt text, assistant output, token-level logs, KV cache entries, session IDs, and request/response headers?
2) For persisted items, what are the default retention periods and what options do we have to reduce those?
3) Can retention be scoped per workspace/customer (we need per-tenant control)?
4) Residency: if we want EU-only storage for prompts/outputs and logs, which deployment modes support that out of the box?
5) Who has access to persisted content inside Redwood operations (engineers, SREs)? Is there role-based access + audit trail?
6) Is there a supported server-side PII redaction workflow or do we need to implement client-side redaction before sending?

Also: please confirm what you consider the minimal telemetry that is kept for hosted by default (what fields, for how long). Our Security team will need the exact field list to complete their questionnaire.

Appreciate a concrete matrix we can attach to our RFP response.

— Lydia
Lydia Chen
Head of Product Security, MedPath
lydia.chen@medpath.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@medpath.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: prompt/output persistence, residency, and retention — next steps & MOP

Lydia — thanks, great questions. Below is the concrete mapping you can give to Security/Legal; I’ve also attached the Excel matrix with the same rows so you can drop it into the questionnaire. If you want, we can run a short workshop with your SecOps next week to walk the matrix.

Concrete mapping (short form):
- Full prompt text:
  - Hosted API: not persisted by default; ephemeral in-flight only. If customer opts into Quality Monitoring (opt-in flag per workspace), prompts are stored for up to 90 days (configurable 0–365). Storage region: US by default; EU-hosted tenants available on request.
  - Dedicated: traces (prompts) persisted by default for 90 days; retention configurable in the contract and via the console (down to 7 days). Region: configurable to your dedicated pool region.
  - Private (VPC/on-prem): persisted only if customer configures storage; Redwood does not ship prompt data out of customer environment unless explicitly enabled.

- Assistant outputs (model responses): same policy as prompts. We treat prompt+response as a single trace for quality monitoring.

- Token-level logs / debug traces (e.g., per-token timings):
  - Hosted: minimal timing telemetry persisted 30 days by default (latency histograms, request counts, no raw token text).
  - Dedicated: full debug traces kept 90 days by default (configurable).
  - Private: controlled by customer.

- KV cache entries: stored in transient caches on the serving nodes; not written to long-term storage by default. For Dedicated/Private you can choose to snapshot caches to persistent storage; snapshots are customer-controlled and typically retained per your retention policy.

- Session IDs / request metadata (timestamps, model used, prompt length): stored as metadata; hosted retains this lightweight metadata for 30 days for billing/observability.

Access & controls:
- Role-based access controls for Redwood staff: engineers/SREs only get access via an audited jumpbox and only for cases where a customer has opened a support ticket and granted session-level access. Every access is logged to the audit trail.
- Customers can request export of all persisted traces at any time; we support SFTP/Push to your cloud storage.

PII handling & redaction:
- Client-side recommendation: if you have direct PII (PHI/SSNs), the most robust pattern is to perform redaction/hashing client-side before sending.
- Server-side: Redwood supports configurable redaction rules at ingestion (regex and pattern-based); redacted copies are stored with original text masked. Server-side redaction is available for Dedicated and Private; Hosted support available as an add-on for POCs.

Encryption & residency:
- All persisted data encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.3).
- KMS integration: Dedicated and Private can use customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS/HSM).
- Residency: EU-only storage supported for Dedicated and Private; Hosted EU regions available (we can map per-tenant).

Defaults and customization summary:
- Hosted default telemetry: request metadata + latency metrics (30 days), no prompt/response persisted unless opted-in.
- Dedicated default: traces persisted (90 days), configurable; audit logs 365 days.
- Private: retention/location enforced by customer.

Next steps (concrete MOP):
1) I’ll attach the retention matrix (row-by-row) to the HubSpot record (link above).
2) Karthik — please confirm whether we can share the full SOC 2 report under the current NDA; if not, we’ll share the summary and provide SOC2 on execution of an NDA.
3) Lydia — confirm residency (US vs EU) and whether you want server-side redaction enabled for the POC.

If helpful I can also produce a tailored CSV listing every field we persist for the Hosted API so Security can ingest into their questionnaire tool.

Best,
Sean

- We would like server-side redaction enabled for the POC (please provide the rule set template).
- Please share the SOC 2 summary now; we’ll execute an NDA if we need the full report.

Monica / Karthik — looping you in from Redwood is fine. Please drop the retention matrix CSV into the Drive link and I’ll forward to Legal.

Looking forward to the workshop.

— Lydia
